children: Real estate has lagged the S&P 500, but October and November of U.S. midterm years have historically been different, with the sector rising in 18 of 25 such periods since 1926, according to SentimenTrader.

SentimenTrader said in a post on X that the sector gained in 72% of those periods, with winning periods averaging a 10.2% return. It cautioned that the pattern is a seasonal tendency, not a call that the sector has bottomed.
The chart showed the historical growth of $1 invested during October and November of midterm years.
The accompanying table breaks out the seven losing periods, which averaged a 7.5% decline. The median gain was 8.7%, compared with a 4.3% median decline in losing periods.

The strongest winning period gained 31.0%, while the largest decline was 26.8%. The sector gained at least 10% in nine of the 18 winning periods and fell by at least 10% in one of the seven losing periods.
